chapter.title: Spare Parts
chapter.note: Rebuilt on 6 November 2026 against the PowerPyx 100% chart (63 boxes, 3 endings, no icons), the detroitbecometext template and string table, and the Fandom wiki. HUNTING FOR PARTS → the crane → the drone (✓/✗) → REACH CYBERLIFE → SECURITY ANDROID APPEARS (ATTACK, GRAB ANDROID AND HIDE, RUN AWAY, HIDE) → GUARD SEARCHES (ATTACK, RELEASE, HOLD POSITION) → RESUME SEARCH → the crate (FREE / LEAVE ANDROIDS) → JOHN WANTS TO JOIN → JOHN MENTIONS KEY → CONTROL ROOM (THREATEN, LURE, BLACKOUT or MARKUS GETS SPOTTED) → STEAL KEY and LEAVE WITH TRUCK, or ALARM SOUNDS → RUN TO FENCE → DOGS MAUL JOHN (LEAVE / SAVE) → three endings. Relationship arrows are the template’s (46 icons); the wiki’s four extra Jericho arrows are not built. Cross-chapter: John joined and came home (Freedom March); the ending label for later media. Researched in docs/research/ch19-spare-parts.md.

decisions.title: Hunting for Parts (checkpoint) to Progress Toward CyberLife
decisions.context: Markus, North, Simon and Josh climb onto the docks at night to steal parts and blue blood for Jericho. North leads them between the containers past dock workers; they are almost spotted by two guards, then cross the container tops.

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: HUNTING FOR PARTS, CLIMB ONTO DOCK, FOLLOW NORTH, ALMOST SPOTTED, CLIMB ON CONTAINERS, PROGRESS TOWARD CYBERLIFE.

decisions.note: Six chart nodes in a line. ALMOST SPOTTED may be optional (PowerPyx: Markus must walk toward the guards).

benchmark.note: One narrated event with the game’s lines. No stat change.

decisions.title: Follow North or Follow Simon
decisions.context: North jumps onto a crate on a crane with Josh and calls Markus up; Simon goes around over the containers.

options.label: FOLLOW NORTH
options.effect: The crane. No stat change.

options.label: FOLLOW SIMON
options.effect: Over the containers. No stat change.

decisions.note: Movement choice; the template has only the condition “Follow Simon”.

benchmark.note: A two-option decision with no effect.

decisions.title: Drone Blocks Path, Neutralize Drone
decisions.context: A security drone blocks the warehouse; Markus plans a climbing route and jumps onto it.

options.label: MARKUS UNHARMED
options.effect: North, Simon, Josh small up.

options.label: MARKUS DAMAGED
options.effect: North, Simon, Josh small down.

decisions.note: A quick-time pair (✓/✗). The wiki also lists Jericho up/down; the template does not.

benchmark.note: One action with a 0.2 risk roll (unsourced). Template arrows only.

decisions.title: Reach CyberLife (checkpoint), Gather Spare Parts
decisions.context: The group gets into the warehouse and starts filling its bags. Simon: “Quick, open the other crates and fill your bags.”

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: Leads to SECURITY ANDROID APPEARS.

decisions.title: Security Android Appears
decisions.context: The security android John catches them; the human guard Mike calls for him and comes closer.

options.label: ATTACK (Kill Guard)
options.effect: Josh large down. Mike dies (MARKUS SPILLS BLOOD); John deviates from the shock.

options.label: GRAB ANDROID AND HIDE
options.effect: John deviates; the guard searches for him.

options.label: RUN AWAY
options.effect: North small down ×2; Jericho, Josh, Simon small down. Alarm, fence, “ran away” ending. Experienced only.

options.label: HIDE
options.effect: John reports four androids; alarm, fence, “ran away” ending.

decisions.note: Chart order ATTACK, GRAB, RUN, HIDE; template labels Kill Guard, Grab and Hide, Run away, HIDE.

benchmark.note: Four options in chart order with the template’s labels and arrows; none can fail (the old 15% and 10% failures are gone).

decisions.title: Guard Searches for Security Android
decisions.context: Mike sweeps the crates with his flashlight while Markus holds John.

options.label: ATTACK
options.effect: Josh large down; Mike dies (MARKUS SPILLS BLOOD).

options.label: RELEASE
options.effect: John covers for them (HUMAN GUARD LEAVES).

options.label: HOLD POSITION
options.effect: Mike misses them (HUMAN GUARD LEAVES).

benchmark.note: Three options in chart order; template labels ATTACK, Release, Hold.

decisions.title: Resume Search (checkpoint)
decisions.context: Back at the crates; a bigger crate stands on a platform. The chart draws a line straight from here to JOHN WANTS TO JOIN.

options.label: Check the bigger crate
options.effect: FIND CRATE OF ANDROIDS.

options.label: Pass it by
options.effect: Straight to JOHN WANTS TO JOIN.

decisions.gate: After the guard is dealt with (ATTACK or GRAB).
decisions.note: The skip edge is on the chart; the unused OVERLOOK CRATE OF ANDROIDS node is not.

benchmark.note: A two-option decision with no effect.

decisions.title: Find Crate of Androids
decisions.context: Three new androids stand inert in the crate. Markus: “Why aren’t you like us? Don’t you wanna be free?”

options.label: FREE THEM
options.effect: North, Simon, Josh small up (no Jericho arrow in the template). Changes Simon’s and Markus’s lines at JOHN WANTS TO JOIN.

options.label: CLOSE AGAIN
options.effect: Nothing.

decisions.gate: If Markus checks the bigger crate.
decisions.note: First on-screen use of Markus’s converting touch (Markus page).

benchmark.note: Template labels and arrows; freeing no longer brings them along (that is ACCEPT).

decisions.title: John Wants to Join
decisions.context: “Take me with you.” North: “We can’t trust him.” Josh: “We can’t just leave him here.” Simon: “It’s too dangerous!”

options.label: ACCEPT
options.effect: North, Simon small down, Josh small up. John joins; JOHN MENTIONS KEY. If he comes home, he sacrifices himself in Freedom March.

options.label: REFUSE
options.effect: John triggers the alarm; fence; full bags if Markus makes it.

decisions.gate: After the guard is dealt with (ATTACK or GRAB).

benchmark.note: Template labels and arrows (North’s down is now applied). Sets john and ch19JohnJoined.

decisions.title: John Mentions Key
decisions.context: John tells them about the trucks of biocomponents and the key in the control station. Simon and Josh say it is too risky; North says they can’t pass it up.

options.label: ACCEPT (GET THE KEY)
options.effect: North, Simon small up, Josh small down. CONTROL ROOM.

options.label: REFUSE (LEAVE)
options.effect: North small down, Josh small up. Fence with no alarm; John comes home.

benchmark.note: Its own decision now (the old M08 merged it with the control-room methods); GET THE KEY’s arrows are applied.

decisions.title: Control Room (checkpoint), Enter Room, Find Key
decisions.context: Markus climbs into the guard station; two guards chat (“Is Mike still in Zone 4?”); the key is on the console. A gun, a screwdriver and oil drums are at hand.

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: Leads to the methods.

decisions.title: Threaten, Lure or Create Blackout
decisions.context: Deal with the two guards or avoid them to take the key.

options.label: THREATEN GUARDS (TAKE GUN)
options.effect: INCAPACITATE GUARDS ✓ (key), KILL GUARDS ✗ (Derek dies, key), TRIGGER ALARM ✗.

options.label: LURE GUARDS (ATTRACT GUARD)
options.effect: AVOID GUARDS (key) or FAIL TO AVOID GUARDS (alarm).

options.label: CREATE BLACKOUT (SHORT CIRCUIT)
options.effect: AVOID GUARDS (key) or FAIL TO AVOID GUARDS (alarm).

options.label: Walk in (MARKUS GETS SPOTTED)
options.effect: Alarm.

decisions.note: Every alarm here carries the template’s “Be seen by the guards” arrows: Jericho ×2, North ×2, Josh, Simon small down.

benchmark.note: Risk rolls (unsourced): threaten 0.3 (below 0.1 alarm, else kill), lure 0.25, blackout 0.2; walking in is certain to be seen. Story 1.9.7: the blackout guards also say “Fuses are over there.” and “I don’t know shit about electricity…” (MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, 0LjHSb_5bLY 54:43).

decisions.title: Alarm Sounds, Run to Fence
decisions.context: Two copies on the chart: after a control-room alarm (to DOGS MAUL JOHN or SUSTAIN DAMAGE REACHING THE FENCE), and after RUN AWAY, HIDE, REFUSE John or LEAVE (to BACK TO JERICHO or SUSTAIN DAMAGE REACHING THE FENCE).

options.label: Reach the fence
options.effect: Dogs maul John (control-room alarm) or back to Jericho.

options.label: SUSTAIN DAMAGE REACHING THE FENCE
options.effect: Markus is damaged and rescued; GROUP FAILED THEIR MISSION.

decisions.note: A timer in the game (“Take too much time”). Markus cannot die here.

benchmark.note: One action with a risk roll (unsourced): 0.15 after an alarm, 0.08 without.

decisions.title: Dogs Maul John
decisions.context: A dog brings John down at the fence. North: “It’s too late. If we go back we’ll be killed too!”

options.label: ABANDON (LEAVE JOHN BEHIND)
options.effect: John dies; GROUP RETURNED WITH FULL BAGS.

options.label: SAVE (SUSTAIN DAMAGE TRYING TO SAVE JOHN)
options.effect: John dies anyway; Markus is damaged and rescued; GROUP FAILED THEIR MISSION.

decisions.gate: After a control-room alarm, if Markus reaches the fence.
decisions.note: John “dies regardless” (wiki John). If Markus never reaches the fence, John is later alive (wiki continuity note).

benchmark.note: Two options in chart order; no arrow on either.

decisions.title: Endings
decisions.context: MARKUS STOLE A TRUCK FULL OF PARTS, GROUP RETURNED WITH FULL BAGS, GROUP FAILED THEIR MISSION; then Markus’s speech in Jericho (two versions).

options.label: MARKUS STOLE A TRUCK FULL OF PARTS
options.effect: Jericho, Simon, North large up; Josh small up.

options.label: GROUP RETURNED WITH FULL BAGS
options.effect: All four small up.

options.label: GROUP FAILED THEIR MISSION
options.effect: Ran away when the guard arrived: Jericho large down, others small down. Markus rescued: Jericho and North large down, Simon and Josh small down.

decisions.note: No ending icon. No public-opinion change (the news reaction is unused content).

benchmark.note: A narrated event applying exactly one of the template’s four Jericho blocks; records ch19Ending (chart label) for later chapters. Story 1.9.7: both speeches are complete, with the sentences earlier shortened by ellipses (MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, 0LjHSb_5bLY 40:46, 18:55).
